english_text: Warm up before exercising and cool down afterwards.
Drink water before, during, and after exercise.
Wear comfortable and supportive footwear when exercising.
Avoid exercising in extreme heat to prevent heat exhaustion.
Listen to your body and rest if you feel pain during exercise.
Consult your doctor before starting a new exercise programme.
Exercise is safe and beneficial for most people with chronic conditions.
Physical activity is recommended for people living with HIV.
Exercise helps people with TB regain their strength during recovery.
Physical activity supports mental health and reduces stress.
Reduce the amount of time you spend sitting each day.
Take short breaks to stand and move during long periods of sitting.
Encourage your children to be physically active every day.
Limit screen time and encourage outdoor play for children.
Physical activity is important at every stage of life.
Older adults should include balance and strength exercises.
Pregnant women can continue moderate exercise with medical advice.
Physical activity after delivery supports postnatal recovery.
Exercise with a friend or family member for motivation and safety.
Join a community exercise group or sports club.
Set realistic exercise goals and celebrate your progress.
Physical activity does not have to be expensive or complicated.
Consistency is more important than intensity when exercising.
Make physical activity a part of your daily routine.
Avoid smoking as it reduces your capacity for physical activity.
Alcohol reduces your motivation and ability to exercise.
A healthy lifestyle combines good nutrition, exercise, and rest.
Sleep is an essential part of a healthy lifestyle.
Adults need seven to nine hours of sleep every night.
Create a regular sleep routine to improve your sleep quality.
Avoid screens and caffeine before bedtime.
A comfortable and dark sleeping environment improves sleep.
Chronic sleep deprivation increases the risk of many health problems.
Stress management is an important part of a healthy lifestyle.
Deep breathing, meditation, and yoga can help reduce stress.
Talking to someone you trust can help relieve stress.
Seek professional help if stress is affecting your daily life.
A positive attitude supports your health and recovery.
Social connections and relationships are important for your wellbeing.
Volunteering and helping others can improve your mental health.
Taking care of your health is an investment in your future.
A chronic disease is a long-term condition that requires ongoing management.
Common chronic diseases include diabetes, hypertension, and asthma.
Chronic diseases can be managed effectively with the right treatment.
Following your treatment plan helps prevent complications.
Regular monitoring of your condition helps detect changes early.
Self-management is an important part of living with a chronic disease.
Learning about your condition empowers you to manage it better.
Diabetes is a condition where the body cannot regulate blood sugar properly.
Type 2 diabetes can often be prevented with a healthy lifestyle.
Managing diabetes requires a healthy diet, exercise, and medication.
Monitor your blood sugar levels regularly as advised by your doctor.
High blood sugar over time can damage your kidneys, eyes, and nerves.
Foot care is very important for people with diabetes.
Check your feet every day for cuts, sores, or changes in colour.
Wear comfortable shoes to protect your feet if you have diabetes.
Hypertension is a condition where your blood pressure is too high.
High blood pressure often has no symptoms and is called a silent killer.
Regular blood pressure checks are important for early detection.
Managing hypertension requires medication, diet, and lifestyle changes.
Reduce your salt intake to help lower your blood pressure.
Avoid stress and get regular exercise to manage hypertension.
Uncontrolled hypertension increases the risk of heart attack and stroke.
Take your blood pressure medication every day without missing doses.
Asthma is a chronic lung condition that causes difficulty breathing.
Asthma can be triggered by dust, smoke, pollen, and cold air.
Identify and avoid your asthma triggers to prevent attacks.
Always carry your reliever inhaler with you.
Use your preventer inhaler every day as prescribed.
Seek emergency care immediately if your asthma attack is severe.
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is a serious lung condition.
Smoking is the leading cause of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
Stopping smoking is the most important step in managing lung disease.
Heart disease is a leading cause of death worldwide.
A healthy diet and regular exercise reduce the risk of heart disease.
Chest pain, shortness of breath, and dizziness may indicate heart disease.
Seek emergency care immediately if you experience chest pain.
Stroke occurs when blood flow to the brain is interrupted.
The signs of stroke include sudden weakness, confusion, and difficulty speaking.
Call for emergency help immediately if you suspect a stroke.
Epilepsy is a condition that causes recurrent seizures.
Take your epilepsy medication every day to prevent seizures.
Inform your employer and family about your epilepsy.
Avoid activities that could be dangerous if you have a seizure.
Mental health conditions such as depression are treatable.
Seek help early if you are experiencing symptoms of depression.
Anxiety disorders are common and can be effectively treated.
Do not be ashamed to seek help for mental health problems.
Mental health treatment may include counselling and medication.
Substance abuse is a health condition that requires treatment.
Seek help if you are struggling with alcohol or drug use.
Rehabilitation programmes are available to support recovery.
Kidney disease can be prevented by managing diabetes and hypertension.
Drink enough water to support healthy kidney function.
Avoid taking too many painkillers as they can damage your kidneys.
Liver disease can be caused by alcohol, hepatitis, and fatty liver.
Avoid alcohol to protect your liver from damage.
Get vaccinated against hepatitis B to protect your liver.
Cancer can affect any part of the body.
Early detection of cancer greatly improves treatment outcomes.
Attend cancer screening programmes regularly.
A healthy lifestyle reduces the risk of many cancers.
Seek medical attention immediately if you notice any unusual lumps or changes.
Osteoporosis is a condition where bones become weak and brittle.
Calcium and vitamin D are important for bone health.
Weight-bearing exercise helps maintain bone density.
Arthritis causes pain and stiffness in the joints.
Physiotherapy and medication can help manage arthritis.
Maintain a healthy weight to reduce pressure on your joints.
Anaemia is a condition where you do not have enough red blood cells.
Iron-rich foods and supplements help treat iron deficiency anaemia.
Seek medical attention if you feel persistently tired and weak.
Thyroid disorders can affect your weight, energy, and mood.
Regular thyroid function tests help monitor your condition.
Take your thyroid medication at the same time every day.
Skin conditions such as eczema and psoriasis require ongoing management.
Protect your skin from the sun to prevent skin cancer.
Use moisturiser regularly to manage dry skin conditions.
Eye conditions such as glaucoma and cataracts can cause vision loss.
Regular eye examinations help detect eye conditions early.
Wear sunglasses to protect your eyes from UV radiation.
Hearing loss can be prevented by avoiding loud noise exposure.
Wear ear protection in noisy environments.
Seek medical attention if you notice changes in your hearing.
Oral health affects your overall health and wellbeing.
Brush and floss your teeth daily to prevent gum disease.
Gum disease has been linked to heart disease and diabetes.
Visit the dentist regularly for check-ups and cleaning.
Every person has the right to access healthcare services.
Healthcare services in public facilities are available to everyone.
You have the right to be treated with dignity and respect.
You have the right to receive care regardless of your background.
You have the right to receive care regardless of your HIV status.
You have the right to receive care regardless of your gender.
You have the right to receive care regardless of your age.
You have the right to receive care regardless of your disability.
You have the right to an interpreter if you do not speak the local language.
You have the right to have your cultural beliefs respected.
You have the right to privacy during your medical examination.
You have the right to a clean and safe healthcare environment.
You have the right to emergency care even if you cannot pay.
You have the right to be informed about the cost of your treatment.
You have the right to complain if you are not satisfied with your care.
You can submit a complaint to the clinic manager or health department.
Your complaint will be investigated and you will receive a response.
You have the right to be protected from abuse by healthcare workers.
Report any abuse or mistreatment by healthcare workers immediately.
You have the right to be involved in your own care plan.
You have the right to accept or refuse any proposed treatment.
Informed consent must be obtained before any procedure.
You must be given enough information to make an informed decision.
You have the right to withdraw your consent at any time.
Children and adolescents also have rights in healthcare settings.
Adolescents have the right to access sexual and reproductive health services.
Confidentiality is maintained for adolescents seeking healthcare.
Older adults have the right to dignified and respectful care.
People with disabilities have the right to accessible healthcare.
Healthcare facilities should be accessible to people with disabilities.
Sign language interpreters should be available for deaf patients.
Braille materials should be available for visually impaired patients.
Mental health patients have the same rights as all other patients.
Involuntary treatment can only be applied under specific legal conditions.
Community health workers provide health services at the community level.
Community health workers can help you navigate the health system.
Mobile clinics bring healthcare services to remote communities.
Outreach programmes provide services to people who cannot access facilities.
Telemedicine allows you to consult a doctor remotely.
Emergency medical services are available for life-threatening conditions.
Know the location of your nearest emergency room.
Keep the emergency services number saved on your phone.
Ambulance services are available for medical emergencies.
Do not use emergency services for non-emergency conditions.
Primary healthcare clinics handle most common health conditions.
Referral hospitals provide specialised care for complex conditions.
Follow the referral process to access specialist care.
Bring your referral letter to all specialist appointments.
The national health insurance aims to provide universal health coverage.
Health insurance helps cover the cost of medical care.
Apply for a medical aid or health insurance if you can afford it.
Social grants are available to support people with disabilities.
Apply for a disability grant if your condition prevents you from working.
The clinic social worker can help you access social support services.
Non-governmental organisations provide additional health and social support.
Faith-based organisations also provide health and social services.
Know your rights and use the health services available to you.
Advocate for better health services in your community.
Health is a human right and everyone deserves quality care.
Taking care of your health is your responsibility and your right.
Empower yourself with health knowledge and share it with others.
A healthy community starts with informed and empowered individuals.
Work together with your healthcare team to achieve the best outcomes.
Your health journey is a partnership between you and your healthcare provider.
Trust your healthcare team and communicate openly with them.
Ask questions until you fully understand your condition and treatment.
Never leave a consultation without understanding your next steps.
Your health is your most valuable asset — protect and invest in it.
Small daily health habits lead to long-term wellbeing.
Every positive health choice you make today benefits your future.
You are capable of managing your health with the right support.
Believe in your ability to improve and maintain your health.
